subject: English
passage: Julia Valdez composed dozens of songs in the 1960s and 1970s. At the time, major record labels rarely signed Latina singer-songwriters, so few of Valdez's songs were professionally recorded. Only a handful of her compositions were published during that period. But that doesn't mean that Valdez never learned what other people thought of her music. Valdez organized monthly gatherings for fellow Latino musicians and composers in her Los Angeles home. Participants would perform and critique one another's work, including Valdez's own. These gatherings could therefore serve as ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: an opportunity for major record labels to discover new talent.
choices.B: a method for Valdez to learn about musical trends in other regions.
choices.C: inspiration for Valdez to write songs in different musical styles.
choices.D: a way for Valdez to receive feedback on her compositions.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer. The passage tells us that participants at Valdez's gatherings "would perform and critique one another's work." This suggests that the gatherings could provide a way for Valdez to receive feedback on her compositions. Notice how the text foreshadows this conclusion by the mention of Valdez learning "what other people thought of her music."
